voyage float32 output_dtype wire-spelling verification
==========================================================================

STATUS:      VERIFIED 2026-08-28 — REJECTED. The wire spelling "float32" is
             NOT accepted. HTTP 400, body verbatim below, which also
             ENUMERATES the accepted set for this model:
             ['binary', 'float', 'int8', 'ubinary', 'uint8'].
Date issued: 2026-08-28T19:58:05Z
Issued by:   the operator holding the Voyage key, from the local
             environment. ONE call, no retry — no second call was issued
             with "float" or any other spelling, because the rejection body
             enumerated the vocabulary and a second call would have been
             spend for a string already printed.
Spend:       one embedding call on a single one-token input. The request was
             refused on ARGUMENT VALIDATION, before any embedding work.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Three places in this repo state that the shape of
Voyage's float response "belongs in a recorded one-time verification", and
../voyage.go stated that the wire-spelling question "is tracked separately".
Before this file, none of that resolved anywhere: there was no float32
counterpart to the ubinary record beside this one, and no ticket under the
float-producer work covering it. An obligation asserted in three comments and
recorded in none is indistinguishable from an obligation nobody holds. This
file is the recorder; it was created ahead of the answer so the three
comments cited something real, and it now holds the answer.

THE PRECEDENT is ful1498_voyage_code4_verification.txt beside this file:
one deliberate call, recorded verbatim with its raw status and body, whose
conclusion changed exactly one claim in the code and nothing else. This file
follows that form.


WHAT WAS UNVERIFIED, precisely
------------------------------

callVoyageBatch used to send the RESOLVED CONFIG'S dtype string straight
through as the request's output_dtype field:

    OutputType: e.Dtype

For a float32 profile that put the literal string "float32" on the wire. The
one prior recorded verification showed the wire value "ubinary" for the
ubinary path, which is a value Voyage's documented output_dtype vocabulary
contains. Whether "float32" was ALSO a value that vocabulary contains is what
was unestablished. The published vocabulary for output_dtype is
float|int8|uint8|binary|ubinary — note "float", not "float32" — so the
spelling this client sent might not be the spelling the provider accepts.

THE CONFIG VOCABULARY AND THE WIRE VOCABULARY ARE TWO DIFFERENT SETS, and
this repo used one string for both. That is the question this file records,
and the answer below is that the two sets genuinely differ.


THE CALL AS ISSUED
------------------

    curl -sS -o resp.json -w '%{http_code}\n' \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data-binary @body.json \
      https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings

body.json (verbatim, exactly as sent):

    {"input":["package main"],"model":"voyage-code-3","input_type":"document","output_dimension":1024,"output_dtype":"float32"}

The key was issued exactly as the precedent file's was: read from the
operator's config, written to a mktemp file under umask 077 and chmod 600,
passed to curl as -H @<file>, deleted immediately after the call. It never
appeared in argv, in shell history, or in any recorded output. The
Authorization header is written above as "Bearer ***REDACTED***".

Raw status: 400

Raw response body (verbatim, 170 bytes — the entire body):

    {"detail":"Value 'float32' supplied for argument 'output_dtype' is not valid -- accepted values for 'voyage-code-3' are ['binary', 'float', 'int8', 'ubinary', 'uint8']."}


ACCEPT / REJECT CRITERION, AND THE GRADE
----------------------------------------

ACCEPT — the spelling this client sent is correct — required ALL of:

    raw status                       = 200
    len(data[0].embedding)           = 1024   (values, not bytes)
    every element is a JSON decimal  = true   (not an integer array)
    model echoed by the API          = the model requested

REJECT — the client sends a spelling the provider does not accept — if the
status is 4xx and the body names output_dtype or its accepted values.

GRADE: REJECT, on the criterion's own terms. The status is 400 and the body
names both output_dtype and its accepted values. A rejection is the LOUD
outcome and is not a data-integrity problem: the arm surfaces it as a
terminal, non-transient llm.LLMError on the first float32 call, so no corrupt
vector was ever produced by this failure mode. What it meant is that the
float32 config surface could not reach Voyage at all until the request-side
spelling was translated.

A 200 whose embedding array held INTEGERS rather than decimals would also
have been a REJECT, and a more interesting one, since the arm cannot detect
that direction — every integer is a valid JSON decimal. That branch is MOOT
here: the request was refused on argument validation and never reached
embedding generation, so nothing about the response representation was
observed and nothing about it is claimed.


WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE
----------------------------------

THE SHIPPED CODE IS NOW CONDITIONED ON THIS RECORD, which the earlier draft
of this file said it was not. ../voyage.go carries two constants where it
carried one: voyageDtypeUbinary/voyageDtypeFloat32 remain the CONFIG
vocabulary (the strings config.AcceptedEmbedDtypes admits, and the strings
the decode branches on), while voyageWireDtypeUbinary/voyageWireDtypeFloat
are what output_dtype carries. voyageWireDtype translates between them at the
one point the request is built.

BOTH WIRE SPELLINGS COME FROM THE BODY ABOVE, not from reasoning: "float" and
"ubinary" are two of the five values that rejection enumerated. No spelling
was invented, and no second call was spent to confirm one the provider had
already printed.

AN UNTRANSLATABLE DTYPE IS REFUSED, NOT FORWARDED. Forwarding whatever the
config held is what produced this 400, so voyageWireDtype errors on any value
outside the two it can name, and callVoyageBatch surfaces that as a terminal
config error before a request is built.

THE UBINARY PATH IS UNCHANGED, byte for byte. "ubinary" is spelled the same
in both vocabularies, so the request body a ubinary profile sends is
identical to the one it sent before the translation existed;
TestVoyageArm_UbinaryRequestBodyUnchanged pins the whole body against a
hand-written literal, and it passed against the pre-change tree as well.

The arm's DECODE path is untouched by all of this and was never in question:
it is verified against canned payloads by TestVoyageFloatBatch, which reads
the response according to the CONFIG dtype the arm carries.

No default model and no default dtype changed as a result of this record.
